items.text: River atlas on the intake desk: title leaf says second edition, 1896. Draft the listing at £48; check whether all foldouts are present.
Mara paid for the river atlas. She needs it at the field station by Thursday. Ask whether the carrier accepts our long flat box.
Back-room heater clicks three times and trips the socket. Leave that outlet unused until the repair visit.
Club on Tuesday: The Small Orchard, chapters 1–7. Five people confirmed; buy decaf and move the returns trolley.
ATLAS / plate count 12 / fold at p. 44 split / pencil £48. Tiny stamp beneath the pastedown: revised issue.
Carrier form for Mara: no signature waiver, flat parcel, declared value forty-eight pounds. Destination contact answers after lunch.
Blue slip: 'Mara, twelve, Thursday?' Nothing else legible.
Correction to atlas listing: the revised-issue stamp belongs to 1901, not 1896. Keep the earlier photo in the provenance folder; change the year before sending a receipt.
Heater repair quote: fan bearing plus labour, £73. We can use the counter socket for the lamp but the failed unit stays unplugged.
For Orchard night, use the question about why the narrator hides the keys. Nobody wanted the printed plot summary last time.

Atlas handoff sheet: catalogue now says revised issue, 1901, twelve plates, one split fold. Copy that condition wording into Mara's enclosure and put the atlas between two boards so the damaged fold cannot flex.
Mara's box fits the carrier's flat rate if we trim the spare board by a centimetre. Do not trim the atlas wrapper.
The engineer found fluff wedged behind the heater fan. Bearing replacement cancelled; clean and electrical test only.
Shelf card proof: RIVER ATLAS — revised issue (1901). Condition note should say 'split fold', not 'missing plate'.
Orchard group now seven; Jo can bring two folding chairs. Leave room by the door for the walking frame.
Sent Mara the tracking code. The field station gate closes at four, so I added that to delivery instructions.
'Can you change it to four?' clipped voice message, no sender recovered.
Heater passed its electrical test this morning. Screw the guard back on before the room is used for stock sorting.
Mara says the flat box arrived dry and all twelve foldouts are there. Close the dispatch ticket.
Orchard discussion went well with the keys question. Keep the seven-chair layout for next month; return Jo's pair tonight.
Donation from the old print co-op: nineteen poetry pamphlets. Give each its own record, even where the covers look identical.
Window plan: a paper moon over three orange crates. Borrow the moon from Suri; she needs it back before the parade.
Elm School wants twelve poetry books under £60 including postage. Teacher asked for short poems suitable for reading aloud.
Receipt roll core reads 12 mm; paper width looks like 57. Measure it before ordering another carton.
Chess manual return, order 57: pages 81–96 duplicated, 97–112 absent. Customer sent these photos and wants a replacement.
Pamphlet checklist: Noon Ferry has eight leaves, not missing pages. Its foldout cover makes it look incomplete. Record the artist's initials exactly as printed.
Elm shortlist has eleven titles. Add Noon Ferry only if the price still leaves six pounds for postage.
Moon will fit in the window if the middle orange crate goes sideways. No books against the glass: condensation yesterday.
57 again. too wide? ring after 2
Replacement chess manual checked page by page; complete. Email the prepaid return label for the defective one.
Count correction for print co-op intake: eighteen pamphlets, not nineteen. Two rubber bands held one long foldout together; it wasn't a second title.
Actual till paper is 58 mm wide, 12 mm core. Previous 57 was an estimate from the squashed roll. Order two boxes of the measured size.

School packing list and stock update: reserve Noon Ferry and eleven other pamphlets for Elm, total £51. Mark those twelve catalogue records sold as a bundle and print the itemized enclosure for their librarian.
Rename the 'Autumn crates' window job to 'Paper Moon'. Same borrowed moon, same orange crates; use the new heading on Suri's return reminder.
Supplier confirms 58 mm till rolls arrive Friday. Keep the current roll's cardboard core as the size sample.
Elm's poetry carton collected. Librarian approved the itemized £51 list; postage was £5.40.
Chess customer chose a refund after all. Stop the replacement before dispatch; refund order 57 when the faulty copy comes back.
Co-op pamphlet records left to finish: title lettering on Salt Steps and the unnumbered white booklet. Use first lines when no title exists.
Paper Moon lit from the left now. Suri's name is on the reverse of the prop so it won't be sold with the stock.
No label on this envelope. 'Hold the white one' written across flap.
Leena's cello: neck projection dropped during rehearsal. Photograph the heel gap before loosening strings; no glue until the joint is inspected.
Tomas asked for black hair on his spare bow, normal length. He'll collect after Saturday's lesson.
Door cylinder sticks even with the spare key. Ordered a replacement keyed alike to three fresh keys.
Leena needs a loan cello for Friday's concert. Call the cooperative about their full-size instrument and check whether a hard case is included.
Heel gap close-up: old hide glue crumbled out dry. Mortise edges intact; neck reset estimate two bench days.
Co-op reply: full-size loan cello available Thursday afternoon, deposit £90. Leena must sign it out herself.
Tomas's frog slide is stubborn. Protect the pearl while opening it for the rehair; keep the removed knot in the job tray.
'90 by Thursday; ask L.' on torn masking tape.
Measured Leena's neck dry-fit again: three bench days, not two, because the button needs reinforcement. Concert deadline will not be met.
Key blanks arrived wrong profile. Locksmith will bring the proper cylinder and matching keys together Tuesday.

Leena repair/loan call: neck reinforcement needs until Monday. Extend the co-op cello booking through Monday evening and set its bridge curve close to her usual setup so the Friday programme is playable.
Bow rehair test for Tomas: at playing tension the ribbon is even, but two loose hairs need trimming near the tip.
Loan cello receipt, Leena: Thursday 15:30 to Monday 18:00, case included. Photograph existing scuff on lower rib at pickup.
Leena neck joint clamped cleanly. Pencil line shows no movement after initial tension; leave overnight before final setup.
Workshop cylinder now turns freely. One new key to the cleaner, one to me, one in the sealed spare envelope.
Tomas prefers slightly firmer tension than the first trial. Re-seat the knot rather than shorten hair at the frog.
Leena played her repaired cello for twenty minutes. Projection stable; invoice should include the button reinforcement.
Bench note without object: 'leave overnight; tiny movement?'
Co-op accepted Leena's loan cello back Monday, matching pickup photos. Deposit released.
Tomas collected the bow after trying the firmer setup. Keep the black-hair preference on his job card.
Museum mandolin has a split beside the treble foot. Strings are off; curator wants stability for display, no promise that it will be playable.
Four folding stands for the quartet. Prototype must fit inside the old bus locker, maximum folded length 62 cm.
Start finish tests for museum mandolin on offcuts. Amber wash over isolation layer; record the mix so the touch-up can later be removed.
Close view under mandolin top: one loose brace stops just before the crack. Pencil marks show where the two cleats may sit.
stand hinge squeaks / drill jig hole wandering / try hand reamer
Finish card: mix amber 3, clear 7. Under cool light it looks too orange next to the mandolin's worn edge.
Curator approved two small cleats on the mandolin split, keeping the stamped date visible. Photograph the stamp before installation.
62? lid won't shut
Quartet bus locker was measured with the lid open. Correct folded-stand limit to 58 cm, replacing the earlier 62; shorten the lower rail drawing.
Mandolin repair test: the amber 3/clear 7 sample obscures grain under exhibition lighting. Retire that recipe; the new card is amber 1/clear 9 over the same isolation layer.
Cleats glued and clamp pressure released. Mandolin seam stays shut with no string load; do not add tension just to prove a display repair.
Finish notebook page for the mandolin: one-to-nine mix stays translucent after drying. Removal test lifts it without disturbing the isolation coat.
Quartet stand prototype folds to 57.5 cm now. Bass player tried opening it one-handed; add a thumb notch in the latch.

Joint review with curator: mandolin seam is stable with two cleats; coat only the pale exposed line using the one-to-nine amber trial. Add both the cleat positions and finish-removal method to the conservation record. We looked at the top first under the bench lamp and then under the warmer exhibition lamp. The repaired line is more noticeable under the bench lamp, but the curator prefers that to covering the surrounding original surface. Leave the little dark scratch beside the treble foot alone; it appears in the oldest photograph and is not part of this damage. Before applying colour, photograph the closed seam with a scale and mark the two cleats on a separate underside sketch. Attach the approved offcut sample number and isolation-coat notes so a future conservator can distinguish our touch-up from the original finish.
Under magnification the mandolin cleats have no squeezed-out glue near the stamp. Conservation photo accepted.
Tin labelled 'clear' has no mixing date. Don't use until identified.
Quartet rails cut as a set of four. One knot at the hinge line: remake that rail before assembling the remaining stands.
Dry mandolin touch-up viewed from normal gallery distance. Curator says the pale line no longer distracts; store the approved sample card with recipe.
Museum signed off the mandolin's stable display condition. Foam support must carry the neck; repaired top should bear no mounting weight.
All four quartet stands fit the locker and open with the new thumb notch. Write the hinge oiling note on their care sheet.
Slate Ridge Saturday: bus to Mill Gate, climb by the eastern path, camp at the old quarry. Seven kilometres carrying packs.
Miso sitter: Ana can do Saturday dinner but needs the key before Friday. Cat food is in the red cupboard.
Tent test in shower: slow drip along the foot-end seam. Mark the wet spot with tape; buy seam sealer.
Ridge food for three: oats twice, lentil packets Saturday night, wraps for lunches. Ben cannot eat sesame.
Friday client report handoff: Jules needs the draft charts by Thursday noon to cover my leave.
Map enlargement shows the quarry is inside the no-camping zone. Revise Slate Ridge overnight stop to Juniper Field; add two kilometres to Saturday.
Tent foot seam cleaned and sealed. Cure flat indoors for a full day before repeating the water test.
Voice memo lost the start: 'three, red one, before Friday'.
Juniper Field has a tap by the gate, but the notice says seasonal. Phone the caretaker before deciding how much water to carry on the ridge.
Ana has the key and Miso's feeding card. She asked me to leave a light on a timer.
Client report charts exported. Jules spotted a missing legend on revenue; fix it before sending the Thursday handoff.

Call with caretaker: Juniper Field tap shut this weekend. Move the route's lunch stop to Mill Spring for a refill, and pack an extra two-litre bladder plus a no-boil dinner so our water plan still works.
Second tent shower test: the foot seam stays dry after ten minutes. Repack only when the fly has dried.
Rename our 'Slate Ridge weekend' route sheet to 'Juniper loop'. It's still the same bus, walkers and revised Juniper Field camp; easier to distinguish from last year's ridge plan.
Lentil packet labels have sesame oil. Replace all three with the chickpea pouches; Ben checked those ingredients.
Miso's sitter backup is Omar if Ana's late shift runs over. Both have the same feeding card; don't double the evening meal.
Jules received the client report with revenue legend restored. Leave note says he owns any Friday edits.
Juniper loop GPX now includes Mill Spring and the extra distance. Download it before leaving mobile coverage.
Green bag by the door. Check whether it has the small one.
Ridge meals packed: sesame-free chickpeas, wraps, oats, extra bladder. Put Ben's marked pouch at the top for the spring lunch stop.
Heron Island overnight permits opened. Request two adults at the north meadow pitch for 18 May; no fires allowed.
Tom's wide bike tyres may not fit ferry rack slots. Send the ferry office a side photo before reserving cycle spaces.
Island sky session: take the small tracker and a 24 mm lens. Want the beacon at the edge of the frame, not in the middle.
Balcony pots dried out last trip. Trial a wick from the big bucket into each herb pot before we leave.
North meadow permit provisional, reference HN-28. Ranger wants arrival ferry time before assigning the pitch.
Ferry says wide tyres go on the floor straps. Two passenger tickets and two cycles held on the 10:40 boat.
Tracker batteries held charge overnight. Run another test with the cold pack; the island can be windy after sunset.
HN? 28? pencil rubbed out below the number.
Herb wick trial flooded the mint tray. Raise bucket to the same level as the pots, not above them.
Ferry timetable correction from office: 10:40 sailing cancelled for inspection. Our two bikes and passengers moved to 12:10; confirmation attached.

Permit update for HN-28: give ranger the new 12:10 ferry arrival plan and request late pitch check-in. Ferry office also needs our camping permit number added to the bicycle group booking; reply to both confirmations.
Beacon test frame from last scouting visit: even the short exposure flares across the centre. Put the camera east of the post and shade the lens with the hood.
Heron north meadow permit issued for two adults, one night. Ranger marked the pitch beyond the hand pump; print the no-fire conditions.
Ferry loading rehearsal: unclip both panniers and tie the front wheel so it cannot turn while the wide-tyre bike is strapped down.
Watering trial day two: mint tray damp, basil upright. Bucket line dropped about one centimetre; mark the full level before departure.
Remember the adapter. It's on the shelf.
Sky forecast note for Heron outing: if haze hides the stars, make a long exposure of the beacon reflection. Pack the neutral-density filter for that fallback.
Heron permit printout now in the dry pouch. Check out with the ranger by ten Sunday so the pitch isn't marked occupied.
Ferry cycle booking shows floor straps for both bikes and the 12:10 departure. Tom has a screenshot for the ticket office.
Tripod feet washed; lens hood and spare tracker batteries in camera pouch. Beacon composition sketch taped inside.
Traverse practice plan: work six closed-loop questions this week, then redo any closure errors without looking at the worked answers.
Surveying exam portal: registration incomplete until photo ID and access-arrangement form are uploaded. Deadline the 14th.
Dental receptionist offered the 14th at 09:00 for check-up. Ask whether that includes cleaning.
Study circle: Mei and Rowan can meet Wednesdays. Reserve the quiet room and give everyone two questions to contribute.
Loop exercise 4: I keep applying the eastings correction to the northings column. Circle the column labels before calculating.
Exam access form sent with evidence. Portal still says pending; save the confirmation number and check Friday.
Wednesday room booking needs a group name. Use 'Survey circle' and book ninety minutes, no projector.
'14, bring the form' on a sticky note without letterhead.
Correction to my traverse formula card: distribute angular misclosure evenly across angles here, not proportional to line length. My previous card mixed two different adjustment steps.
Dentist confirmed the 14th appointment includes cleaning. Appointment card says arrive ten minutes early for updated history form.
Rowan's proposed study questions duplicate Mei's. Keep Mei's two and ask Rowan for instrument-error problems before Wednesday.

Bring my corrected angular-misclosure card to the Survey circle and run a ten-minute worked example. Add the six traverse questions I practised to the shared bank, with the eastings/northings mistake highlighted in the answer notes.
Exam centre approved a low-distraction seat. Registration is complete once I pay the remaining fee by Monday.
Timed traverse attempt: 42 minutes, closure within tolerance. Still wasted five minutes copying coordinates twice.
Quiet-room staff moved our Survey circle to upstairs room 2 for this Wednesday only. Send the room number with the question sheet.
Portal receipt: exam fee paid, low-distraction seat noted, candidate entry saved offline.
Too early. move to next week?
Dental visit done. Next routine check-up card filed; buy the smaller brush heads recommended during cleaning.
I redid loop exercise 4 from blank paper. No swapped columns this time; annotate the old wrong solution rather than deleting it.
Survey circle attendance five. The short worked example fit; leave more time for everyone's instrument-error answers next meeting.
Records certificate drills: fifteen retention scenarios each morning. Error log heading is 'Red list'; explain why I chose the wrong category.
Kitchen shelf bracket spacing 44 cm. Wall detector flags a cable on the right, so don't drill until the route is checked.
Ask training coordinator to reimburse the records certificate fee. Policy wants a paid receipt and manager's approval, even before the result.
Mock exam on Sunday: 80 questions, 100 minutes. Print one clean answer sheet and put the phone outside the room.
Library card expires this month. Renewal desk needs current address proof; electricity statement will do.
Retention drill: deletion freeze overrides the routine disposal date when a hold applies. My answer assumed the schedule kept running.
Manager approved exam expense. Finance rejected the bank screenshot; download the provider's itemized receipt.
Exam mock booklet erratum: this edition has 75 questions and a 90-minute allowance, replacing my 80/100 setup. Reprint the timer cover.
'Use current statement' torn corner, no logo.
Shelf cable runs vertically from the socket. Move both brackets left by 8 cm; shelf still clears the kettle lid.
Rename my 'Red list' study log to 'Reasoning repairs'. Same scenario errors; new heading reminds me to write the rule instead of just circling mistakes.
Library renewal accepted with electricity statement. New expiry date is next September; keep the same physical card.

Sunday mock finished in 88 minutes, 58 of 75 correct. Wrong answers cluster around legal holds and duplicate record copies. Don't judge progress from the raw score until the answer-key erratum is checked.

Mock review: after checking the erratum, score is 60/75. Copy the remaining hold and duplicate-copy errors into Reasoning repairs; schedule ten fresh scenarios in those categories for Tuesday, and annotate the mock answer sheet with the corrected key.
Finance received itemized exam receipt and manager approval. Reimbursement queued for next payroll under training, not travel.
Kitchen shelf installed level. Kettle lid clears by three fingers; let the adhesive screw covers settle before wiping.
Tuesday drills: nine out of ten holds/copies scenarios right. The miss was an active working copy, not a duplicate record.
Receipt? the one with the old number.
Payroll line 'professional development' matches the full records exam fee. Mark reimbursement complete.
Keep the marked Sunday mock paper as the baseline. Next full mock will use a fresh booklet and the corrected 90-minute limit.
Spanish market practice: ask for half a kilo, ask the price, then understand the answer without switching languages.
Receipt photo: rear brake cable, 1.6 mm. Bike shop says bring the old housing when collecting.
Radio Patio lesson 12. Heard the numbers but lost the street names. Replay the weather segment at normal speed tomorrow.
Evening Spanish cancelled; Alma's email offers a credit. I paid 84 and want the money returned instead.
Alma corrected my market card: use the polite request first. Keep the stallholder's likely reply on the reverse.
12 / Alma / green one?
The cable is fitted but the rear lever still reaches the handlebar. Check tension before riding to work.
Refund form sent with the course receipt. Cancellation date is the 18th, not the 8th as I wrote in my first email.
Radio Patio: the presenter said fourteen, not forty. I copied the transcript too soon; listen blind once before checking it.
Market target update: stop rehearsing half-kilo orders. The stalls sell by the piece here; ask for three tomatoes and two peppers.
Call this notebook section Stall conversations now; it used to be Market speaking. Same cards, just a name I will recognize.
Alma says accounting approved the 84 refund; allow five working days. Save the message until the bank entry appears.
Practice clip: I order three tomatoes, then pause while the seller answers. Still saying the question as one long word.

Use Patio's produce interview for two exercises: transcribe the seller's prices for listening practice, then turn those replies into my stall-conversation cards. I need both the audio timestamps and the spoken prompts.
Rear brake passes the slow driveway test. Trim cable tail and fit an end cap before calling the repair done.
Patio episode 13 has two voices overlapping. Save it for Friday; twelve is now understandable without the transcript.
Ask again on Friday. They may have changed it.
Market debrief: managed the order, but needed the price repeated. Add one short request for repetition to the stall cards.
Bank screenshot: course repayment 84 received. The cancelled evening class claim can be closed.
Patio listening log: street names 4/6 today, numbers 6/6. Next replay without slowing playback.
Kitchen handles: photograph the hole spacing before ordering. The current brass finish is flaking.
Saturday Polish circle homework: six sentences with instrumental endings. Olek will check the plural forms.
For Grandpa's Polish interview, begin with his school kitchen story. Aim for ten minutes, with permission to pause whenever he wants.
96 mm between the kitchen handle holes. Need twelve replacements, including the narrow drawer.
Case-drill sheet: I keep using the singular ending after two friends. Circle the noun and rewrite each example aloud.
Grandpa wants the interview in the morning; he gets tired after lunch. Ask about the school cook before moving to the railway job.
Return the twelve handles: I measured the outside width. Actual screw centres are 64 mm, checked against the paper rubbing.
Olek's audio feedback on my instrumental exercise: endings mostly right, stress misplaced in the second example. Repeat slowly, then naturally.
The kitchen one first, then the difficult bit.
Interview question card, large print: Who worked in the school kitchen? What did you carry home? Leave room beneath each for a follow-up.
Matte nickel handle sample looks less yellow under our kitchen light. Try it on the drawer before buying the other eleven.

I brought Grandpa's interview questions to the Polish circle. We will correct the noun cases together, keep the corrected question cards for recording day, and add the mistakes to my weekly drill sheet.
Study circle moved from plurals to place expressions. Homework is describing a room; my cabinet handles can stay out of the sentences.
Recorded interview test: fridge hum overwhelms Grandpa's voice in the kitchen. Move the recorder and chairs to the sitting room.
Six location sentences read without looking. Olek marked only the last case ending; rewrite that one before Saturday.
Kitchen handle order confirmed: twelve at 64 mm, matte nickel. Old screws are too long for the new fittings.
Grandpa recording completed: fourteen minutes about school meals, seven about his first job. He asked me to cut the neighbour's surname from the family copy.
Nickel sample / Saturday / ask Olek?
All kitchen handles installed. Put two spare short screws in the labelled fittings bag.
Family interview export checked with Grandpa: surname removed, his school cook story retained. Send the audio privately to his daughters after he approves this cut.
Pantry shopping cap 38 this week. Need oats, lentils and rice; check unopened bags before paying for duplicates.
Tiny webbing inside the flour seam. Empty that shelf, seal the affected flour for disposal, and inspect the adjacent packets.
Water bill uses estimated reading 0038. Photograph the actual meter and send it with account reference Cedar Flat.
Soup swap on Sunday: six lentil portions in returnable tubs. Tessa brings bread; I need to mark mine dairy-free.
Jar label design: ingredient, opened date, best-before. Use blue washable marker on plain paper for the first trial.
Inspection update: oats are infested too. Add replacement oats and flour to the shopping list after clearing the contaminated packets; leave the sealed rice alone.
Actual water meter reads 0029, not the estimated 0038. Portal photo uploaded, waiting for a revised bill.
38, blue, back shelf
Oats cheaper in the large sack, but the small sealed bag fits this week's pantry budget and our containers. Buy one, not three.
Label soak test failed. Replace the plain paper and washable ink with waterproof tape and permanent black lettering; keep the three fields.
Vacuumed the empty pantry shelf corners and washed the bins. Record any new moth sightings each evening for two weeks.
Soup trial too thick after chilling. Reserve cooking liquid so Sunday's six tubs can be loosened before collection.
Water account reply: revised charge issued using the uploaded meter photo. Check next month's opening reading is 0029.
Pantry receipt total 31.70. Flour, oats and lentils purchased; rice crossed off because the unopened bag was usable.
Cut twenty waterproof jar strips. Large lettering reads well through the cabinet glass; dates need two extra blank squares.
Six soup lids say lentil, dairy-free, made Sunday. Tessa will collect four tubs; hold the other two for Ivo.
Pantry watch, evening nine: no moths on shelf or wall. Keep monitoring until the full two weeks are done.
The replacement is on the table. Check before Friday.
Jar label tape survived the second wash. Finish the rice and oats jars with opened dates from their packets.
Soup swap complete. Four empty tubs returned already; note that Ivo still has two, for the next collection.
Breakfast plan for the next fortnight: overnight oats on workdays, toast at weekends. Inventory the oats before placing the grocery order.
Shared oil order, sheet 27: Rina 2 litres, us 3, Mo 1. Supplier quoted delivery for one six-litre carton.
Seed packet photo: balcony salad mix, batch 27, sow shallowly. Check whether both window boxes get enough morning light.
We have three breakfasts' worth of oats, no raisins. Add a kilo of oats and one small raisin bag to the household order.
Mo corrected the oil sheet: wants two litres, not one. Total is seven; ask whether we can combine a six-litre carton and a bottle.
Breakfast delivery arrived crushed. Oats split across the wet carton; photograph parcel and labels for a courier claim, and put replacement oats on tomorrow's breakfast shopping list.
Use the shallow tray for salad seedlings, not the tall empty pot. Balcony gets sun until ten; move the tray away from the dripping outlet.
Courier claim K-27 opened. They need the delivery timestamp and a clear image of the split breakfast-oats packet.
27 — one more? Rina has the picture.
Oil supplier accepts seven litres at the same unit price. Collect on Wednesday; bring clean bottles and a funnel for splitting the carton.
Replacement oats bought locally. For tomorrow's breakfast soak just two portions; the children chose toast this week.
Uploaded the damaged-carton photos to K-27. Claim value excludes the intact raisin bag; only the spoiled oats are being claimed.
Oil cost table checked against seven litres: split delivery by household, contents by volume. Rina paid her share today.
Salad seedlings showing at the tray edge. Rotate the tray each morning so they stop leaning toward the balcony rail.
Breakfast note: oats with chopped apple were popular. Reduce the next raisin order; the small bag remains nearly full.
K-27 accepted for the spoiled oats. Courier offered store credit, but the claim form requested repayment to the original payment method.
Wednesday oil split done. Mo took two filled bottles; the remaining three litres on our shelf are the household allocation.
Thin the balcony salad seedlings to leave a finger's width between them. Save the packet for the next sowing date.
Breakfast cupboard checklist pinned inside door: oats below one jar triggers purchase; check fruit bowl before adding dried fruit.
Courier repayment appeared today for claim K-27. Save confirmation with the damaged parcel photos and close the claim.
Fern Quarterly cover brief: one fern curling around a teacup, cream background, space above for the masthead. First sketch due Tuesday.
Invoice draft FQ-18: cover illustration 420, payable within thirty days. Need the publisher's billing address before sending.
Portfolio front page feels crowded. Replace the old grid with six large images and a short commission enquiry link.
Cat sitter Mara can visit Saturday and Sunday. Send feeding amounts and show where the spare key lives.
Fern sketch feedback: cup handle should face left. Keep the leaf silhouette; editor liked the breathing room above it.
FQ-18 billing address received. Editorial contact and accounts contact differ; send the invoice to accounts with the approved fee attached.
Mara / cream / Tuesday
Fern editor correction: no teacup after all. Replace it with a plain seed envelope; retain the curled fern and cream field. Tuesday sketch deadline still stands.
Portfolio image shortlist: harbour print, winter orchard, moth study. The new six-slot layout needs a mix of editorial and personal work.
Rename the Fern cover folder to Spring seed cover. This is still the same Quarterly commission, following the teacup-to-envelope brief change.
Cat-care sheet: half a pouch each morning, dry food after the evening visit. Mara tested the key; it sticks unless lifted slightly.
Spring seed cover approved. Export the print TIFF at the editor's dimensions and send the signed approval to accounts so invoice FQ-18 can be released today.
Portfolio contact button is unreadable on the moth thumbnail. Move the enquiry link beneath the image grid.
FQ-18 sent for 420; thirty-day due date entered in the ledger. Do not count editor approval as payment received.
Cover export check: tiny white seam at the seed envelope edge. Re-export the print file and replace the proof attachment.
Fern art can appear in my portfolio only after the issue launches. Schedule the Spring seed thumbnail for that date and retain the editor's permission email.
The one on the left is approved. Send when ready.
Mara's Sunday cat photo: bowl refilled and key returned through the letter slot. Pay her for both visits.
Accounts remittance names FQ-18, amount 420. Matched it to the bank entry; the cover invoice is settled.
Six-image portfolio live. Tested the enquiry link on a phone; the Spring seed slot stays unpublished until the issue date.
Lantern Steps visitor map: show the canal entrance, three stages and accessible toilets. Deliver a landscape sheet suitable for folding.
Tablet pen pressure drops to zero halfway through strokes. Test a new nib before buying another pen.
Festival stickers: four lantern-bird poses, bold outlines and no tiny feet. These are individual cut shapes, not map icons.
Monthly billing list: Lantern Steps map 600; Kelp magazine spot 160; stickers still awaiting scope confirmation. Invoice numbers start at 600 this month.
Lantern Steps draft license grants print use for this year's festival. Ask whether they also need website display and merchandise resale.
Map walk-through: canal gate is locked during performances. Put visitor entrance on Hill Lane and remove the canal entry arrow.
Sticker bird looking back reads as a broken neck. Rotate the whole body and keep the beak visible in the next sheet.
600 / bird / signed? bottom unreadable
New nib did not fix pressure loss. Tablet behaves normally on the borrowed laptop; send driver version and a short fault recording to support.
License reply: include festival website for one year; exclude resale of the bird stickers until the merchandise fee is agreed.
Map proof printed at actual size. Toilet symbols disappear in the fold; move them five millimetres inward and enlarge the key.

Festival call decisions, recorded before I forget: finalize all four sticker poses with a white border. The sleepy bird's wing must stay inside the cut shape, and the standing one needs a wider gap between its legs so the backing does not tear. They now want to sell these at the information stall, rather than give every sheet away. Add the agreed resale permission to the illustration license, covering only this festival's printed sticker run. Any later reprint needs another discussion. Include the extra 90 merchandise fee in this month's invoice round and describe it explicitly, because their bookkeeper could otherwise mistake it for another drawing charge. Send the revised sticker proof and rights paragraph together for approval before exporting the cut files.
Invoice 600 is the Lantern Steps map, not an amount paid. It remains open; Kelp's 160 payment cleared this morning.
Support's tablet driver rollback restored pen pressure. Keep the failing version number in the ticket until two full drawing sessions pass.
Four lantern-bird stickers exported with the white cut border. Print one sheet to check the backing separates cleanly.
Signed festival license received: annual website use and the priced sticker resale clause are present. Archive the signed copy and countersign.
Hill Lane map approved after the folding test. Send the final landscape PDF and an unfolded proof image to the festival printer.
Same issue as last time. Try it without the extra bit.
Tablet ticket closed after two complete pressure-sensitive drawing sessions. Keep automatic driver updates off until checking the next release notes.
Month-end ledger: map invoice 600 paid, sticker invoice still outstanding including its 90 rights fee. Send one polite reminder for that balance.
School rapid entries close Thursday. Five rounds, twenty minutes each side; collect age group and emergency contact on registration.
Hall sketch: eighteen chess tables in three rows, clocks on the aisle side. Leave the rear doorway clear.
Trophy engraving proof: School Rapid, winner and runner-up for each age group. Check the year before approving brass plates.
Boiler annual service booked with Deni for Thursday, window 9–12. Clear the cupboard shelf so the panel opens.
